source_name: ČNB — České a vybrané mezinárodní asociace na finančním trhu
why_relevant: The regulator's own curated index of Czech financial-market associations — banking (ČBA), credit unions (ADZ), insurance (ČAP, AČPM, ČSpA, KSLPU), capital markets (AKAT, ČASF), pensions (APF ČR) — each with its website. This is the authoritative pointer-of-pointers that guarantees the association layer of the map is complete and not invented.

source_name: ČNB – Seznamy a evidence (supervision lists hub)
why_relevant: Hub page that enumerates every list ČNB publishes (JERRS, WS JERRS, open data, prospectus registers, rating agencies, other lists). Best single entry point for snowballing to all regulator-maintained pointer sources; an EN mirror exists at /en/supervision-financial-market/lists-registers/.

source_name: ČNB – Číselník kódů platebního styku v ČR (ČKPS / bank codes) a Číselníky, seznamy, registry
why_relevant: The bank-code codelist is the join key between institution names, IBANs and clearing participation, and the hub page also carries the list of payment systems, foreign settlement-system participants, and comparison-website operators under §202 of the Payments Act. Indispensable for entity resolution across all other CZ payments sources.

source_name: ČNB – Platební instituce a instituce elektronických peněz (legislative/regulatory base)
why_relevant: Defines the CZ licence taxonomy (PI, IEP, PPSMR, VEPMR) that any competitor-set model must mirror, and links out to the corresponding registers and rules. Essential for correctly bucketing register entries into payments market segments.

source_name: ČNB – Ostatní seznamy (other supervisory lists: payment systems, covered-bond issuers, comparison sites)
why_relevant: Long tail of niche but high-signal official lists: 'Seznam platebních systémů', foreign settlement/payment-system participants, operators of comparison websites under §202 of the Payments Act, and the list of activities under the limited-network exclusion (which enumerates closed-loop/gift-card style payment schemes normally invisible in registers).

source_name: ČNB – Informační povinnosti subjektů finančního trhu / Co nového v dohledu
why_relevant: Enumerates the reporting obligations each licence category owes ČNB — which tells you what data exists about each competitor, in what granularity and cadence, and therefore what may become publicly derivable. The companion 'Co nového v dohledu' feed is the running change-log of supervisory expectations.

source_name: Portál gov.cz — Registr smluv service page (publication mechanics)
why_relevant: Explains the publication workflow, metadata schema and legal exemptions — needed to know what is systematically missing (e.g. contracts exempt from disclosure) before drawing coverage conclusions.

source_name: Portál gov.cz – rozcestník stížností na finanční instituce
why_relevant: Official signpost mapping which complaint body handles which payment dispute type (ČNB vs finanční arbitr vs ČOI); useful to enumerate the full CZ complaint-channel landscape for this cell.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) — seznam členů a přidružených členů
why_relevant: Complete enumeration of the licensed Czech banking sector (~32-35 members representing >99% of the market), split into full members (banks and branches of foreign banks with a ČNB licence) and associate members (representative offices and banking auxiliary organisations). The associate-member tier is the highest-value part for vendor scouting: it is where non-bank service providers to banks appear.

source_name: cz-banking-psd2 – community list of Czech bank developer portals (GitHub)
why_relevant: A maintained index mapping every Czech bank to its developer portal URL — the single best snowball seed for enumerating CZ bank API docs, sandboxes and the platform vendors behind them.

source_name: Temenos Customer Success Stories library
why_relevant: Vendor-owned, filterable index of named bank references; enumerates CEE/CZ clients and dates deployments. One page yields multiple Czech actors and product names (Transact, Core, Data Hub).

source_name: APEK – Asociace pro elektronickou komerci + data.apek.cz
why_relevant: CZ e-commerce association (founded 1998) with a member directory and a data portal covering online payments, e-shop counts and market share. Membership list is a POINTER to gateways/PSPs active in CZ e-commerce; the data portal gives market context for payment-method mix.

source_name: APEK — Asociace pro elektronickou komerci, Seznam členů
why_relevant: 580+ members: e-shops (the merchant demand side for payment acceptance) plus the vendors that serve them — payment gateways, PSPs, logistics and e-commerce platforms. The merchant enumeration is the acquiring-side counterpart to the ČBA bank list. APEK also runs the 'APEK Certifikovaný obchod' programme with its own separate member listing.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe — Reference (CZ site)
why_relevant: Czech-language vendor reference list; the classic 'one page enumerates a dozen clients' pointer. Asseco's banking segment names Česká spořitelna among customers; the CZ site also lists public-sector and financial references.

source_name: Shoptet Partneři – integration request marketplace
why_relevant: Directory of implementation partners and integration offers (e.g. PayU, Klarna gateway integrations). Reveals which gateways are being demanded/implemented and which agencies serve the acquiring ecosystem — a second-order partnership layer banking sources never show.

source_name: CIOtrends / CIO Business World — soutěž Případová studie
why_relevant: Annual competition in which Czech ICT suppliers submit their reference projects with customer names; multi-year archive is effectively a longitudinal register of who implemented what for whom, including financial-sector clients.

source_name: Comgate – nápověda / e-shop platformy a integrace
why_relevant: Comgate's own documentation enumerates every e-commerce platform, accounting package and POS system it integrates with (Shoptet, WooCommerce, PrestaShop, Magento, Shopify, Pohoda, Money S3, ABRA FlexiBee). This is a machine-enumerable partner/integration directory that reveals the whole CZ e-commerce vendor ecosystem around one of the largest domestic gateways.

source_name: CzechTrade – Czech fintech delegations and Czech Fintech Industry catalogue
why_relevant: State export agency organises and then publicly reports CZ fintech delegations to CEE markets (Budapest, 10-11 June 2026), naming the participating companies (e.g. Citfin, Comgate) and the host banks/investors met. It also publishes a Czech fintech industry catalogue PDF — effectively an official, vetted vendor roster for the cell's actor map.

source_name: CzechTrade — Czech fintech industry overview (PDF)
why_relevant: State export-agency directory of Czech fintech and banking-technology vendors — a curated actor list produced by an organisation whose job is to enumerate exporters. Good for discovering payment/banking software houses missing from the seed actor map.

source_name: eForms SDK / eForms metadata reference (TED Developer Docs)
why_relevant: Defines the field schema of modern TED notices (business terms BT-xxx: winner name, winner national ID, contract value, subcontracting, framework agreement flags). Without this the structured notices cannot be parsed reliably. It is also a pointer to which intelligence attributes are actually available per notice — e.g. whether subcontractors and consortium partners are disclosed, which matters for mapping partnerships.

source_name: ICT UNIE — Členové ICTU
why_relevant: Enumerates the Czech IT supplier base that serves banks and the public sector — Aricoma, Asseco Central Europe, Asseco Solutions, DXC, Deloitte Advisory, ICZ and similar system integrators. This is the vendor/competitor bench for banking IT delivery in CZ. English mirror at /en/ictu-members.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) — činnost a členové
why_relevant: The Czech card-payments professional association — banks and other organisations interested in developing payment cards and coordinating related work, with regular membership limited to financial institutions. Historically the venue where card-scheme, acquiring and terminal topics were coordinated; also a source of card-market statistics. Two co-existing domains observed (bankovnikarty.cz and bankovni-karty.cz) suggest a legacy/possibly dormant web presence.

source_name: Vhodné-uverejneni.cz — contracting-authority profile directory
why_relevant: One of the certified Czech 'profil zadavatele' hosting services. Acts as a pointer: given an ICO you can locate a buyer's publication profile and thereby the full tender documentation behind a terse TED notice. Snowballing across profiles enumerates state and state-owned buyers relevant to payments (ministries, Česká pošta, customs administration, state treasury).

source_name: AKAT ČR — Asociace pro kapitálový trh, Členové asociace a Orgány
why_relevant: Capital-market members: asset managers, investment firms, banks (Česká spořitelna appears as a member) and their advisers (law firms such as BBH sit in the association's bodies). Adds the investment/wealth segment of financial institutions and their service providers, which the banking and fintech associations only partially cover. Structured member-detail URLs make it machine-friendly.

source_name: AmCham Czech Republic — Membership Directory (corporate)
why_relevant: Enumerates US-linked and multinational corporates in CZ, including financial-services players (Citibank appears on the board). The board of directors list is itself a who's-who of country managers. Committees and 'Plus Club' groupings indicate which firms lobby on digital/financial policy.

source_name: apiportal.cz – Czech banking API portal aggregator
why_relevant: Local-language aggregator of CZ bank API portals; gives current status of each bank's PSD2/premium APIs and is the natural entry point for enumerating developer portals in Czech.

source_name: Asociace penzijních společností ČR (APF ČR) a Asociace družstevních záložen (ADZ)
why_relevant: Two remaining association slots from the regulator's own index: pension management companies (APF ČR) and credit unions (ADZ, asociacedz.cz). Both enumerate small but distinct classes of regulated financial institutions that buy core systems and payment connectivity, completing the CZ financial-institution census beyond banks, insurers and asset managers.

source_name: ASPPS ČR — Asociace poskytovatelů platebních služeb České republiky
why_relevant: The only association found that is specifically dedicated to payment service providers (non-bank PSPs / platební instituce) in CZ; it states it represents PSP interests toward the legislature, ministries and state administration. Directly on-topic for the payments workstream, though the site appears small/possibly dormant (plain http, .eu domain) so membership depth is unverified.

entity_name: British Chamber of Commerce Czech Republic
source_name: British Chamber of Commerce Czech Republic — Members Directory
why_relevant: 200+ member companies, UK-linked; relevant for UK fintech/payments vendors entering CZ and for professional-services partners. Smaller than AmCham but with a distinct membership tail; board page names the active corporate participants.

source_name: Chambers Global Practice Guides — Fintech: Czech Republic
why_relevant: Annually refreshed English legal-market overview of the CZ fintech/payments landscape written by local counsel — reliable for regulator names, licence categories, market structure and actor mapping that feed better queries elsewhere.

source_name: CPV (Common Procurement Vocabulary) taxonomy as a discovery pointer
why_relevant: The CPV code list is itself an intelligence asset: choosing the right code set (e.g. 72212443 banking software development, 48xxxxxx software packages, 30123600 coin-handling/cash devices family, 66xxxxxx financial services, 72xxxxxx IT services, 50xxxxxx repair & maintenance) determines whether an entire class of Czech banking/payments contracts is seen or missed. Codes also let one enumerate adjacent contract classes not on any prior checklist.

source_name: Czech ICT Alliance — členové (CzechTrade export alliance)
why_relevant: ~160 Czech ICT companies organised as a CzechTrade-backed export alliance (Asseco Solutions, Cleverlance, ICZ, Komix, Sophia Solutions, plus CZ arms of Cisco, HP, Intel, Microsoft). Complements ICT UNIE by highlighting which local IT suppliers are actively export-oriented — i.e. the most likely regional competitors for banking IT deals.

source_name: European e-Justice Portal – Business Registers Interconnection System (BRIS)
why_relevant: Single EU entry point (live since June 2017) into all Member State business registers plus Iceland/Liechtenstein/Norway, with EUID identifiers, cross-border branch and cross-border merger notifications. The route from a CZ subsidiary of a payments vendor to its foreign parent's home register — and vice versa. Note it exposes only basic harmonised data, not filings or financials.

source_name: FeaturedCustomers / Cuspera vendor case-study aggregators
why_relevant: Third-party mirrors of vendor case studies; they retain studies vendors have deleted and normalize them per vendor, making them a recovery route for withdrawn CZ references. Low authority, high pointer value.

entity_name: Gartner Magic Quadrant / Forrester Wave coverage of banking & payment-hub platforms
source_name: Gartner Magic Quadrant / Forrester Wave coverage of banking & payment-hub platforms (incl. secondary pickup)
why_relevant: Vendor placement in the Gartner MQ for Banking Payment Hub Platforms and Forrester digital-banking landscapes is the standard competitive frame vendors use in CZ tenders; press pickup of placements is free and gives the vendor field even without a licence.

source_name: GlobalData company profiles (Czech banks)
why_relevant: Aggregated English profiles of CZ banks with deal history, technology initiatives and competitor sets — an aggregator view that no Czech source assembles; also the data layer behind Retail Banker International reporting.

source_name: Hospodářská komora ČR — struktura, začleněné živnostenské a oborové asociace
why_relevant: ~17,000 members organised in 57 territorial chambers and ~140 sector associations; the Czech Fintech Association states it is a member. The list of incorporated sector associations is a second, independent enumeration of the association layer, and regional chamber sites publish their own member lists (useful for the merchant long tail outside Prague).

source_name: Mambu partner ecosystem directory
why_relevant: Partner directories enumerate the SIs and technology partners that actually deliver CZ projects (Deloitte, Persistent, Backbase et al.); combining vendor + SI names yields far better CZ-specific search recall than vendor name alone.

source_name: openbankingtracker.com – Czech Republic provider index
why_relevant: Third-party index of ~165 CZ providers with their API/developer-portal status; an efficient way to enumerate the long tail of CZ banks, credit unions and PSPs whose developer artefacts should be watched.

source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách (portal-vz.cz) — MMR methodology & NIPEZ hub
why_relevant: Official hub explaining how NIPEZ / VVZ / profily zadavatele / NEN interlock, which forms exist and what must be published where. Essential to design a complete crawl and to know what evidence is legally guaranteed to exist. Also hosts annual state-of-procurement reports and a decisions database.

source_name: SEND.cz / Periodik.cz — Bankovnictví magazine back-issue archive
why_relevant: Subscription vendors expose per-year issue listings and tables of contents for Časopis Bankovnictví, allowing historical topic/vendor mapping and targeted purchase of specific back issues without a full archive licence.

source_name: Shopify App Store – Czech payment gateway apps (cs locale)
why_relevant: International platform marketplace that lists CZ-specific gateway apps (GoPay, Comgate). Cross-checks the Shoptet directory and shows which Czech PSPs invest in reaching merchants on global platforms — a partnership-strategy signal.

source_name: SOCR ČR (Svaz obchodu a cestovního ruchu) — Členská základna
why_relevant: Retail and hospitality confederation — the physical-POS merchant side (grocery chains, retail, gastro, accommodation). Its members include other associations (e.g. APEK itself is listed as a member with a detail page), so it is a pointer-of-pointers into the merchant ecosystem that buys card terminals and POS.

source_name: SPIR — Sdružení pro internetový rozvoj, Členové
why_relevant: Members are the Czech internet economy: publishers, media and creative agencies, technology companies, operators and e-commerce projects. Useful for the digital-marketing/adtech and e-commerce adjacency of payments, and for identifying who runs the digital channels of banks and merchants. Executive council composition signals sector power structure.

source_name: Svaz průmyslu a dopravy ČR (SP ČR) — Členská základna / odvětvové svazy
why_relevant: Top-level confederation whose collective members ARE the sector associations — ČBA, Česká fintech asociace and ICT UNIE all appear with their own SP ČR profile pages. Because SP ČR profiles restate each association's identity and contacts, it works as an independent cross-check on association existence and as a discovery surface for associations not yet on the map.

source_name: Wikipedie – Bankovní identita (cs) as a glossary/actor-map bootstrap
why_relevant: Low-credibility but high-yield pointer: consolidates the member-bank list, official entity name (Bankovní identita, a.s.) and terminology variants (Bank iD / BankID / bankovní identita) used to expand search coverage. Every fact must be re-verified against primary sources.

source_name: Česká asociace pojišťoven (ČAP) — Řádní členové
why_relevant: Full enumeration of Czech insurers — the insurtech/bancassurance counterparty set and a distinct buyer group for payments, billing and core-system IT. Relevant to 'sector=both' coverage where banking and insurance overlap (bank-owned insurers, embedded insurance in payments).

source_name: Česká fintech asociace (ČEFTAS) — Členové (regular + affiliate)
why_relevant: The single best enumeration of the Czech fintech/insurtech/regtech scene. Two tiers: regular members (fintech solution providers — GoPay, ComGate, Twisto, Dateio, MONET+, Wultra, Zentity, Coinmate, BudgetBakers etc.) and affiliate members (Visa, Mastercard, ING, Deloitte, law firms, banks) — i.e. the ecosystem AND its sponsors/partners in one place.

source_name: Česká kryptoměnová asociace (ČKMA)
why_relevant: Represents Czech crypto-asset businesses and users. Under MiCA this is the association layer for CASPs — a set of payment-adjacent firms (exchanges, custody, on/off-ramps) that no banking or fintech association fully enumerates, and a likely counterparty for banks on debanking and MiCA compliance topics.

source_name: Česká leasingová a finanční asociace (ČLFA) — Seznam členských společností
why_relevant: ~35 members covering the non-bank financing market: leasing, consumer credit, instalment sales, factoring (claimed ~86% business financing, ~83% consumer financing, ~95% factoring share). Enumerates captive finance arms (BMW FS, Ayvens, Arval) and independent lenders — a segment of payment/lending IT buyers that banking associations miss. Each member has its own detail page (/spolecnosti/<slug>).

source_name: ČNOPK / AHK Tschechien — Česko-německá obchodní a průmyslová komora a databáze nemeckefirmy.cz
why_relevant: The largest bilateral chamber in CZ (~700 members) and operator of a company database of ~1,500 German firms active in the Czech market (nemeckefirmy.cz), in Czech and German. Useful for identifying German-owned banks, captive finance arms and IT suppliers operating locally — a group the domestic associations under-represent.
